pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/auth/require-operator.ts:24 In open mode every request counts as the operator. There is no check that Host, X-Forwarded-Host or Origin name loopback. `next dev` (scripts/dev-guard.mjs passes no host) and `next start` with KP_ALLOW_OPEN=1 listen on every interface. Server-side calls spend the operator's ambient Claude CLI login, so any LAN peer or DNS-rebound page that reaches the port gets operator-gated routes.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/auth/require-operator.ts:24 Open mode lets everything in with no loopback Host/Origin/forwarded-for gate and no loopback-only bind. proxy.ts:181 enforces only when a password is set or prod fails closed. open-entry.ts isLoopbackHost decides only the landing labels.
app/_lib/auth/session.ts:88 The browser carries the session back sealed with HMAC-SHA256 under KP_SECRET, bound to workspace/sub/role, with exp and epoch inside the payload.

app/_lib/auth/session.ts:52 The signing secret is an unprefixed, server-only env value. It is read in a node:crypto module that cannot be bundled for the client. No NEXT_PUBLIC_ value anywhere in app/_lib/auth.

app/_lib/auth/require-operator.ts:73 The refusal is closed and identical whether the session was missing, tampered, revoked or belongs to a disabled account (the proxy uses the same single refusal shape).
app/_lib/auth/session.ts:105 This context issues and checks the session. It forwards to no upstream.
